blocks.md: Range XOR l..r = f(r) ^ f(l−1). O(1) replaces million-element loops — memorize table shape, derive once on paper.

blocks.label: builtin toolbox (GCC)
blocks.code:
__builtin_popcountll(x)   // ones count (64-bit)
__builtin_ctzll(x)        // trailing zeros = index of LOWEST set bit
__builtin_clzll(x)        // leading zeros (→ MSB position = 63-clz)
__builtin_parityll(x)     // ones-count odd?
// C++20: std::popcount/countr_zero/bit_width <bit>
blocks.py:
# builtin toolbox (Python equivalents):
x.bit_count()          # popcount (Python 3.10+)
(x & -x).bit_length()-1  # ctz = index of lowest set bit
x.bit_length() - 1       # MSB position (guard x>0)
bin(x).count('1') % 2    # parity
# Python ints unbounded: no clz/ctz UB on zero for bit_length
